title: Outage: orders-api in CrashLoopBackOff after a config change

lines.text: 10:00 alert: orders-api rollout not progressing; new pods in CrashLoopBackOff
checkout: every call to orders-api fails (no ready endpoints)
10:40 flash sale: checkout error rate 18% with 3 of 4 orders-api pods

sources.cite: Kubernetes documentation (v1.37), Pod Lifecycle: container restarts and CrashLoopBackOff
sources.note: Relevant text: 'After containers in a Pod exit, the kubelet restarts them with an exponential backoff delay (10s, 20s, 40s, …), that is capped at 300 seconds (5 minutes).' 'CrashLoopBackOff state: This indicates that the backoff delay mechanism is currently in effect for a given container that is in a crash loop, failing and restarting repeatedly.' Steps: check logs, 'Use kubectl describe pod <name-of-pod> to see events', 'Ensure that the Pod configuration, including environment variables and mounted volumes, is correct'. restartPolicy 'The default value is Always.' Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-11.

Relevant text: 'ConfigMaps consumed as environment variables are not updated automatically and require a pod restart.' Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-11. Whether a crash-looping container picks up a corrected value on its own next restart is not modeled (FLAG): the scenario asks for the documented pod restart.

Relevant text: 'when you roll back to an earlier revision, only the Deployment's Pod template part is rolled back'; 'kubectl rollout undo deployment/nginx-deployment'; 'A Deployment's rollout is triggered if and only if the Deployment's Pod template (that is, .spec.template) is changed'; maxUnavailable and maxSurge default to 25% ('at least 75% of the desired number of Pods are up', 'at most 125%'); progressDeadlineSeconds 'defaults to 600'. Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-11.

Relevant text: '-p, --previous: If true, print the logs for the previous instance of the container in a pod if it exists.' Example 'kubectl logs -p -c ruby web-1'. Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-11. The application's own log line and the kubectl output layouts in the scenario are authored renderings.

brief.situation: You are the cluster administrator at Fernhill Books (fictional). At 09:55 a teammate edited the ConfigMap orders-config and ran kubectl rollout restart on the orders-api Deployment (4 replicas, default rolling update) in namespace shop to pick it up. At 10:00 the rollout is stuck: new pods are in CrashLoopBackOff, three old pods still serve. A flash sale starts at 10:40 and needs all four. Find the cause and finish the rollout without taking checkout down.
handover: orders-api reads its settings from orders-config through envFrom. The Service orders-api targets port 8080.
The teammate is in a meeting until 11:00.
howItWorks: Run commands from the command line: type one, or pick it from the suggestions or the action list. Only this lab's commands run; there is no free shell, and each command's arguments come from its list.
Each command takes operator time: run it, then let it finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. The outage keeps developing on the same clock.
The map shows each host, device or service and the links between them, with a status in words. Output appears in the terminal as it happens.
When you declare the service restored, you write the incident record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: How many operator minutes each command or change takes, and when the fictional outage spreads, are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values. The flash sale starts at 10:40, 40 minutes after the alert.

writeup.question: For the incident record: what CrashLoopBackOff told you, how you found the cause, and why your fix worked where a rollback would not.

parts.label: Reading the status
parts.criteria: Explains CrashLoopBackOff as the kubelet backing off restarts of a container that keeps exiting (exit code 1 here), and that the logs of the previous instance say why.
parts.modelAnswer: CrashLoopBackOff means the container keeps exiting and the kubelet is waiting longer between restarts. describe showed exit code 1, so the app quit on its own; kubectl logs --previous showed it rejecting LISTEN_PORT 8O80.

parts.label: Why not undo
parts.criteria: States that rollout undo reverts only the Pod template, not the ConfigMap, so it cannot fix a bad value read through envFrom.
parts.modelAnswer: rollout undo only restores the previous Pod template; the ConfigMap is a separate object, so the old template still reads the bad value.

parts.label: Fix and verify
parts.criteria: Corrects the ConfigMap to 8080 (the Service's target port), restarts the rollout so pods pick up the environment, keeps old pods serving, and verifies the endpoint; proposes validating or versioning config changes.
parts.modelAnswer: I set LISTEN_PORT to 8080, matching the Service, and ran rollout restart, since env from a ConfigMap is read only when a container starts. The rolling update kept three pods serving until the new ones were Ready; wget to the Service answered ok. Next time, roll config out as a new versioned ConfigMap with the Deployment.

criteria.label: Read the previous container's logs before changing anything

rows.when: not isNull(logsPrevAt) and (isNull(firstChangeAt) or timeAt(logsPrevAt) <= timeAt(firstChangeAt))

rows.why: The log was read only after a change.
The crashing container's own output was never read.

criteria.label: Fixed the ConfigMap rather than relying on rollout undo

rows.why: The value was corrected and a restart picked it up.
An undo came first, which cannot change a ConfigMap.

criteria.label: Kept old pods serving: no pod-wide delete, no wrong port

rows.why: A wrong port or a delete-all cost time or a minute of errors.
Every pod was deleted while the value was still wrong.

criteria.label: Verified the Service answers from inside the cluster
Recorded the cause and a lesson accurately

rows.why: The cause is right; the lesson is not.
The record does not match what happened.

reasoningCriteria.label: Written status reading, undo and fix

expertPath.text: kubectl get pods: two new pods in CrashLoopBackOff, three old ones serving. describe: exit code 1, envFrom orders-config.
kubectl logs --previous: LISTEN_PORT 8O80 is not a valid port. The ConfigMap has the typo; the Service targets 8080.
Edit LISTEN_PORT to 8080, rollout restart, watch the rollout complete, wget the Service from a client pod.
Record the ConfigMap typo; roll config out as a new versioned ConfigMap with the Deployment next time.

fixed.headline: Good: fixed at the ConfigMap
fixed.body: You read the crashing container's own last words, fixed the value it rejected, and let the rolling update replace pods while the old ones kept serving.

fixedGaps.headline: Fixed, with gaps
fixedGaps.body: orders-api is healthy. The criteria show the detour: an undo, a wrong port, a delete-all or a late start.

checkoutDown.headline: Checkout down
checkoutDown.body: Deleting pods does not change what they read. While the ConfigMap is wrong, every replacement crashes; the old pods were the only ones serving.

saleFailed.headline: The sale ran short
saleFailed.body: kubectl logs --previous names the bad value in a minute. The fix was one edit and one restart.

stillBroken.headline: Closed too soon
stillBroken.body: rollout undo restores the Pod template, not the ConfigMap; the new pods still crashed.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: CrashLoopBackOff with exit code 1 means the application quits at start. kubectl logs --previous shows it rejecting LISTEN_PORT 8O80 from orders-config. rollout undo would restore only the Pod template, which reads the same ConfigMap. Set LISTEN_PORT to 8080 (the Service's target port), run rollout restart because env from a ConfigMap is read only at container start, let the rolling update replace pods with the old ones serving, and verify through the Service.
